card.title: Merciful Lie
card.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

mechanism: A shields B from an inedibility judgment by recasting the cake as display work and taking over contact with the bakery.
confusable: Unlike empty praise, A must preserve the protective story when B's next action could expose the painful truth.
comparison: D15-a intercepts a bakery inquiry; D15-b publicly signs a euphemistic endorsement to protect a writer's confidence.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
